# Oh
> Oh is open-source memory for agents that stores each fact with its sources and every change in a history you can replay.

Oh ships as a CLI, a TypeScript SDK, and an Agent Skill, and by default it keeps records and the append-only log of every change in one local SQLite file. It is free and MIT licensed and needs no account or hosted model; the CLI runs on Bun 1.3.14 or newer.

## Pages
- [Oh](https://oh.computer): The homepage follows an illustrative review from a research question to a brief through the linked records Oh keeps for each source, claim, and citation. It also reports Oh’s results on the LongMemEval-S, CloneMem, and LoCoMo memory benchmarks, including a comparison with Supermemory, explains how Wordcell uses Oh, gives the install commands, and answers common questions, such as what a passing verification proves.
- [Oh ontology specification](https://oh.computer/spec): The versioned specification defines what an independent implementation needs to interoperate with Oh. It covers the canonical JSON encoding and SHA-256 digests of records and revisions; SQLite and libSQL storage with operation-level sync; and semantic search, Datalog rules whose answers carry proofs, and composite agent memory.
- [Oh benchmark results](https://oh.computer/benchmarks): Every published Oh memory benchmark, including LongMemEval-S, LoCoMo, CloneMem, and a matched pilot against Supermemory, with each study’s headline scores, run date, main limit, and a link to its full record in the repository.
- [Oh comparisons](https://oh.computer/compare): One table sets Oh beside Mem0, Supermemory, Zep and Graphiti, Letta, and Anthropic’s Claude memory tool, says which to pick for which job, and links the pages comparing Oh with Mem0 and Supermemory.
- [Oh vs Mem0](https://oh.computer/compare/mem0): Mem0 is a memory layer that gives a product per-end-user memory through its hosted Platform or a self-hosted Apache-2.0 SDK, while Oh keeps an agent’s own working memory in a local SQLite file with its sources on each fact. The page reports the one matched run so far, on 30 questions in the third-party MemEval harness, and says who should pick which.
- [Oh vs Supermemory](https://oh.computer/compare/supermemory): Supermemory is a hosted memory API with sync connectors and per-user container tags on metered plans, while Oh is local MIT-licensed memory for an agent’s work. The page reports the repository’s matched 60-question LongMemEval-S pilot, where Supermemory scored higher by a margin the pilot could not separate from a tie, and what each system does that the other does not.
- [Oh blog](https://oh.computer/blog): Release announcements, benchmark reports, and technique articles on how Oh works and how it is tested.

## Articles
- [Reading every user message beat retrieval alone on LongMemEval-S](https://oh.computer/blog/longmemeval-s-user-log): The benchmark report explains a pipeline that gives GPT-5 mini every message the user wrote plus the assistant replies retrieval ranks highest. It averaged 93.07% over three runs on all 500 LongMemEval-S questions, against 88.87% for Oh semantic retrieval and 86.13% for BM25, but its rules were written after studying those questions, so the score is in-sample. It also covers the six additions that lowered the score, a reference answer found in the instructions, and what the study cost.
- [Oh tests its Rust encoder byte for byte against TypeScript](https://oh.computer/blog/oh-rust-typescript-parity): The technique article explains how property-based tests compare Oh’s opt-in Rust encoder with the TypeScript reference on thousands of generated inputs, and why the tests must also confirm that the Rust engine loaded, including from an installed package. It also covers number formatting, where the two languages differ by default, and what the tests do not prove.
- [Built on Oh](https://oh.computer/blog/built-on-oh): The hub lists the two Hraness products that use Oh, Sponge and Wordcell, what each uses it for, and when a project needs Oh or Wordcell.

## Optional
- [sitemap](https://oh.computer/sitemap.xml): Every indexable page on oh.computer.
- [blog feed](https://oh.computer/blog/feed.xml): An Atom feed of the blog’s articles.
- [specification index](https://oh.computer/spec/manifest.json): JSON that names the current specification version and links each version’s documents, schemas, and digests, along with the optional research-packet profile.
- [example citation record](https://oh.computer/examples/evidence-table-2.json): The version 1 evidence record from the homepage example, which cites table 2 of a trial report in support of an assertion and carries its dependencies and SHA-256 digest.
- [Agent Skill](https://github.com/hraness/oh/blob/main/skills/oh/SKILL.md): Instructions a coding agent follows to operate Oh through its CLI or SDK, including when to ask the user before choosing a database, space, or sync destination.
- [GitHub](https://github.com/hraness/oh): Source code, the README with install and SDK guides, releases, and issues.
- [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@hraness/oh): The published @hraness/oh package.
